transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Um... I hope I answer this right. 

I came in mostly because... well, my family and friends are kind of frustrated with me. I don't want to sound like a bad person or cause trouble, I really don't, but... we've been having this disagreement for over a year now. 

See, I just know they've been hiding my money. They keep showing me all these bank papers and telling me they prove nothing was taken, but... well, I can tell they're using things like regular bills, and fundraisers, and plans for trips to just cover it all up. 

I really hate upsetting them, but I just feel like I have to keep confronting them—well, asking them about it, really—until they finally tell the truth. I just want to get it all sorted out so we can stop arguing. Does that... does that make sense, Doctor?
Have you ever heard or seen anything that other people around you couldn’t?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I... I don't have anything like that happen. I know some folks hear voices or see things, but I don't. I just see the regular things, like the papers they show me. Nothing that isn't really there. I promise my mind is perfectly fine that way. 

I hope that's... I mean, is that the kind of answer you needed? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being helpful for you.
How certain are you that your family is hiding your money?

Um... I really don't want to sound stubborn, Doctor. I know it makes me seem like a difficult person when I don't just agree with them, and I really hate being difficult. But... I'm completely sure. 

Like I was saying a minute ago, they keep waving those bank papers at me, saying it proves nothing was taken. But I've known for over a year now. I just know they're hiding it. I can see exactly how they use everyday things—like the regular bills, or a school fundraiser, or plans for a trip—to just cover it all up. 

I promise I wouldn't keep confronting them if I wasn't totally sure, because I really, really hate upsetting everybody. I just need them to tell the truth so we can finally fix it. Does... does that make me sound awful? I'm just trying to be honest with you, since you asked. I hope that's an okay answer.
Have you generally been suspicious of other people or their motives for as long as you can remember?

Oh, um... no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always tried to be really trusting and see the best in everyone. I don't want you to think I'm the sort of person who goes around looking for trouble or doubting people just for the sake of it. 

I've always gotten along fine with folks, really. It's just... well, it's just this one thing with my family and the money. Before this started last year, we never had any problems like this. I promise I'm not a suspicious person generally. I just... I just want this one thing to be honest. Is that... does that sound like a normal way to be? I hope it doesn't make me seem paranoid or anything, because I'm really not.
Before this started, did you usually worry a lot about having a serious illness?

Oh, no. No, I never really worried about being sick. I've always been pretty healthy, thank goodness. I try to take good care of myself so I don't end up being a burden on anybody, you know? 

I definitely don't sit around thinking I have some terrible disease or anything like that. I just... I try to stay positive about my health. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, is that what you were hoping to hear? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay with all these questions and giving you what you need.
Do you also tend to mistrust or suspect other people in general, not just your family about the money?

Oh, um... no. I know you asked something kind of like that just a minute ago, and I really don't mind you asking again! But no, I don't suspect other folks at all. 

I trust my neighbors, and the people at the store... everybody, really. I always try to be friendly. I'd feel just terrible if I went around doubting strangers or my friends. That wouldn't be very nice of me, would it? It's really, truly just my family and what they're doing with my money. Everything else is completely fine. 

I hope I'm making sense? I'm trying really hard to be helpful and give you the right answers. I just don't want you to think badly of me.
If your family showed you clear proof that no money was missing, would you be able to accept that you might be mistaken?

Oh, um... I really, really wish I could just say yes to that, because I hate arguing and I don't want to seem stubborn. I want to be agreeable, I really do. But... well, they actually have tried to show me things. 

That's actually why I came in, because my family and my friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken at all. And I know it probably sounds bad of me not to just accept it, and I hope you don't think I'm awful, but... for over a year now, I've just known they're hiding my money. They use all these things to cover it up, like saying it's for regular bills, or these fundraisers, or making up trip plans. 

It makes me feel just terrible to keep bringing it up, and I don't want to cause trouble, but I feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. I'm just trying to stand up for what's right, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult or mean... does that make sense to you? I really want you to understand where I'm coming from.
Outside of this money issue with your family, do you find yourself often suspicious that other people may be trying to deceive or exploit you?

Oh, no, I... I really don't. I'm sorry, I know you asked something like that a little bit ago, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But no, outside of my family and the money, I don't think anyone else is trying to trick me or use me. I try to be trusting of people. I always assume the best in folks, because I think if you're good to people, they'll be good to you. I'd hate to be the kind of person who goes around suspecting everyone of doing bad things. That just wouldn't be right, would it? 

I really do get along fine with everyone else. I hope you believe me. I'm not trying to be a difficult person or anything. Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Before this started, did you usually find it hard to trust people and expect that they might use or deceive you?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I know we've talked a lot about trusting people just now, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same kind of answer again. I just want to be completely honest with you. 

Before all this family stuff started, I was always very trusting. I think I've always been a pretty open person. I never really worried about people trying to use me or lie to me. I've always just wanted everyone to get along and be happy. I try to be a good friend and a good neighbor, and I always figured people would treat me the same way. 

I'd feel just awful if I was the type of person who was always suspicious of everyone before they even did anything wrong. That's not me at all. I hope that's the right answer? I'm really trying to make sure I'm giving you what you need to understand me.
If your family showed you undeniable proof that the money was never taken, would you still believe they were hiding it?

Oh, um... I feel like I might be repeating myself, and I really, really don't want to test your patience. I know you asked something very similar just a few minutes ago, and I hope you don't think I'm ignoring what you're saying. I want to be a good patient, I really do.

But... well, like I mentioned before, they actually *have* tried to show me things. That's the whole reason I'm here, because everyone—my family, my friends—they all keep pointing to these bank papers and saying it proves nothing was taken. And I know it must sound so stubborn of me, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just being difficult, but... I just *know* they're hiding it. 

Even if they showed me more papers, I just... I know it's been going on for over a year. They're so clever about it, using all those regular bills and charity fundraisers and made-up vacations to cover their tracks. I feel terrible even saying it, because I don't want to be the kind of person who causes trouble, but I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally admit it. I hope you can understand why I feel like I have to do that? I'm just trying to get to the truth, I promise. Am I making sense? I really hope I'm not frustrating you.
Have you ever had other unusual beliefs or experiences, like thinking you have special powers or that events around you have hidden personal meanings?

Oh, goodness, no... I don't... I don't have anything like that. No special powers or... or thinking things have secret meanings. I'm just a regular person, I promise. I would never make up stories like that. 

That sounds a little... well, it sounds like something from a movie, doesn't it? I'd hate for you to think I'm the sort of person who imagines strange things like that. I just have this one real situation with my family and the money, but otherwise, I'm completely normal. I just take things exactly as they are, I don't go looking for hidden messages or anything. 

Is that... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really am trying my best to be a good patient for you.
Have you ever heard anyone else explain the missing money in a way that makes you think it could be a misunderstanding rather than theft?

Oh, um... well, I really hope you don't think I'm just ignoring people when they try to explain things. I try to be open-minded, I really do. And I know my family and friends mean well when they keep showing me those bank papers and saying it's all a misunderstanding. They say the papers prove nothing was taken, and... and I'd love to just believe them and make everyone happy. I really would.

But... oh, I hate to sound so disagreeable, but it's just that I've known for over a year now that they're hiding it. They're just so careful about it, you know? Using regular things like bills and charity fundraisers, and making up trip plans to cover up where the money is actually going. 

I've listened to their explanations, I promise I have. I just... I feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally just tell the truth. I don't want to be a bother to anyone, but I just can't let it go when I know what's happening. I hope you don't think poorly of me for that? I just want things to be honest. Am I explaining that okay?
Has this belief about your family hiding your money been the only fixed belief like this, or have you had other similar beliefs too?

Oh, um... no, just this. I really, really hope you don't think I make a habit of... well, of accusing people of things. I know how bad that would look, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just a suspicious person. 

It's just this one situation with my family and the money. I've never had any other... um, I think you called it a fixed belief? I've never had anything else like that at all. I usually get along with everyone so well, I promise. I try to be very easygoing and helpful. I would never just go around making up other stories or causing trouble for no reason. 

I hope you believe me? I just want you to know I'm telling the truth about this one thing, but otherwise my life is completely fine and normal. I don't have any other problems with anyone. Did I... did I answer that the way you needed? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Before last year, did you tend to be a very private or guarded person who found it hard to confide in other people?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm a secretive person, or... or sneaky or anything like that. I've always been very open. I like to think of myself as friendly, actually! 

Before all this happened, I was an open book. I'd talk to almost anyone and share whatever was on my mind. I've always thought it's important to trust people and be honest with them, so I never really had a hard time confiding in folks. I've never been the type to hide away or keep things bottled up. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just want to make sure you know I'm trying to be completely open with you right now, too. Is there anything else you need me to explain about that?
Before this money problem started, would you say you generally tended to be suspicious of other people’s motives?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, that I'm paranoid or always looking for the bad in people. I know that wouldn't sound very good, and I really don't want you to think of me that way.

Before they started taking the money, I always tried to see the best in everyone. I always assumed people meant well. I... I never used to second-guess why someone was doing something nice, or wonder if they had some hidden agenda. I just took people at their word. I think it's so much nicer to live that way, don't you? 

I really try to be a trusting, positive person. It's just... well, it's just this one specific thing with the money that's been so hard. But generally, no, I'm not suspicious at all. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I usually am.
Have you ever had trouble keeping close relationships because you were too suspicious of people?

Oh, no, I've never had trouble with that. I really hope you don't think I'm the kind of person who pushes people away. I value my friends and relationships so much. 

I've always been able to keep close friends, and... well, I've never lost a relationship because I was too suspicious or anything like that. I'm actually a very loyal friend, I promise. I try to be the kind of person people can rely on, and I've always had people I could rely on too. 

It's really just my family and this... this thing with the money. That's the only issue I've ever had. With my friends and everyone else, everything is completely fine. I really hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure you know I'm usually very good with people. Am I explaining that alright?
Before the money issue started, did you usually suspect that people were being dishonest or had hidden motives toward you?

Oh... um, no. I know we just talked about something kind of like that, so I really hope I'm not doing a bad job explaining myself to you. I'm sorry if I am! But no, I never used to think people were being dishonest or... or had secret reasons for doing things. 

I always just believed what folks told me. I really don't want you to think I'm the sort of person who goes around thinking everyone is out to get them, because I'm really not. It's truly just this one awful thing with my family and the money. Everything else before that, I just... I trusted people. 

Is it okay that I'm answering like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need and that I'm not being confusing.
Have you ever believed that something impossible or highly implausible was happening, like being specially targeted by secret agents or having your thoughts controlled?

Oh my goodness, no. Um... no, never anything like that. I really, really hope I haven't said something to make you think my mind is... well, playing tricks on me or anything. Secret agents or people controlling my thoughts? No, I promise my thoughts are completely my own. 

I know how bad that sort of thing sounds, and I would tell you if it was happening, I really would, because I want to be a good patient and help you figure everything out. But I've never thought anything strange like that. It's truly just... just the situation with my family taking my money. That's the only thing. Nothing like spies or anything impossible. I'm just a normal person, really. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that problem? I just want to make sure I'm answering right and that you don't think badly of me. I'm doing okay explaining things, aren't I?
Before last year, did you have a pattern of being distrustful of people or questioning their loyalty in close relationships?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never been like that. I really hope it's okay that I'm just a very trusting person? Like I said before, I've always had good friends and... and I've always trusted them completely. 

I would never want to be the kind of person who constantly questions if people are loyal or... or doubts them. That sounds so awful, doesn't it? I promise I've never had a pattern of anything like that. Before all this started with my family and the money... I was just a regular person who believed in the people around her. 

I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record! I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and that you know I'm trying my best to be helpful. Does that make sense? I'm not being too repetitive, am I?
Before last year, did you ever tend to suspect that your partner, close friends, or other people you depended on might be cheating on you or betraying you?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... no, I've never worried about anything like that. I really hope I'm not sounding, um, too defensive or anything? I just... I've always been very trusting in my relationships. 

I've never had any reason to think anyone was cheating on me or betraying me before this whole awful thing with the money started. I know I keep bringing that up, and I'm so sorry if it's annoying! I just want to be really clear that, um, before my family did what they did, I never had any problems trusting people. 

I really hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'm trying so hard to be a good patient and give you all the right information. I'm doing okay, right?
